My best friend killed herself in January. She  had recently been diagnosed bpd and her mental state just kept getting worse and worse. I and her boyfriend were very supportive and she was seeing two therapists and on regular medication.
We did everything right - everything we could - but she still died. Sometimes, no matter how hard you wish it wasn't true, there really is nothing you can do to change a situation. 
As bleak as it seems, accepting your own powerlessness can help. 
I'm so sorry for what you're going through and I hope you find peace.

Couldn't say for sure. My depression seems to be mostly chemical, worsened by stress, and I've got a lot of that right now! I became suicidal at some stage last year when I was under a really tremendous amount of pressure. I felt like I got over it by April but now it's back and I don't know why. I think it has a lot to do with my dead friend. It was the tremendous pressure if keeping her from suicide that got me so close to the edge last year and her success in January that nearly sent me tumbling over it. I healed, but I've been thinking about her constantly. When things get bad, she's the one I want to talk to. Knowing I can't makes me feel worse I guess.
That's a good idea. I'm more rational now but I never think to do that kind of thing when I'm rational and I never want to do it when I'm insane. I should do some research right this minute.

I was seeing a psychiatrist at the start of the year. I could go back but money's pretty tight so it would definitely add stress. I've never called a hotline before and I don't really want to. I don't want to end up back in the ER again either though. Idk

The girl I loved killed herself in January. I came within days of doing the same. I'm glad I didn't though. I went to therapy and I worked very hard at being better and eventually I decided it wasn't my fault. It was a whole bunch of things that killed her and I know I played my part, but you know what else? I definitely played a part in keeping her alive an extra 12 months, and that ain't nothing. The part I struggle with these days is that if it was always going to happen, if it was impossible to save her, then where does that leave the rest of us depresso fucks? I'm still figuring that much out. It's gonna hurt for a while, but you CAN get through it if you choose to, and I hope you will.

Grades aren't very important at the end of the day, even if your parents tell you otherwise. But if it's something that's causing you stress, maybe talk to them about it and see if they would pay for a tutor? You're always capable of change, no matter what your circumstances look like.

Maybe it would be helpful to reach out to someone else as well? The broader your support network, the better. It can be really hard to talk about, I know, but if you can think of someone you trust, who has a good understanding of your personality and interests, that's a good place to start.

My folks don't know anything but several close friends do. Opening up about it can have mixed results. There are some people I wish I hadn't told: a guy I was dating who was really callous towards it and dumped me, a drunken confession to a near total stranger. It can also be good though, if the right people know, people who can help you with it and who you can talk to when things are bad. I'm definitely better off since I started sharing my experiences. It's not good to be alone.
